name: The Ascent: The Conversation, review pass
thesis: Ask what graduates did in one real moment, how it was arranged, who framed it, who made or recommended the call, and what the feedback was about, not how much A2A developed them. Every answer at a branch point costs the same, so no answer is the shortcut. Images sit only on the two show cards. The open question comes straight after the moment it asks about, and the sponsor's core question sits in the first third. All recall comes before any automation or AI wording. The AI questions follow one neutral picture of meeting prep at five rungs, in which every rung shows who catches the same planted error, and ask where the next Analyst could start each task and still learn.

consistencyPairs.construct: STAGING CHECK on readiness timing, two formats, ten cards apart. h1_first is a dated relational first (a client first called you, not your Advisor; tap stops 1-5). three_year is how the three years felt (tap stops 1-5). The flag is three_year 'Ready at one' (1) with h1_first 'After A2A' or 'Not yet' (4-5): ready after a year, yet no client came to you directly in three. The reverse, 'Year one' with three_year >= 4, is coherent (a client can call before you feel ready) and is reported, not flagged. 'Not yet' respondents are reported separately.

LINKED FIELDS, per task, never quoted back. pack and research appear on both cards. A task swiped 'Mostly grew me' is read against the highest rung at which the respondent thinks the next Analyst could start it and still learn to catch the page-nine error. 'Grew me' placed on 'I set it up once' or 'It's a service' is the case to look at: either the respondent thinks the learning survives there, or the answer is staged. Reported, not used to exclude.

STAGING CHECK, blue token against stem 4, unprompted. pace routes to the wrap_one_* variant for the respondent's blue area, which lists that area as option id 'blue' among five other changes. The token is never mentioned. Choosing it unprompted counts as consistent. The six variants merge into one field.

HYPOTHESIS TEST, not a staging check (Adam's EQ hypothesis). Both cards ask about the best Advisors the respondent has worked with, not about the respondent, so the answer is an observation rather than a self-description (Denrell 2003; evidence finding 11). Where the three stars go is set against whether those Advisors mostly arrived with or built each trait. Reported as a perception. No combination is inconsistent, so this pair never flags anyone.

LINKED FIELDS FOR CONTEXT: stated versus revealed preference on classroom. faster places three afternoons a month that the desk loses; class_mandatory asks whether classroom should be protected from desk deadlines. Afternoons on classroom with 'No, keep it optional' is a divergence to report, not a flag. class_kept asks the same thing, worded from the faster answer, with the same option ids; the two merge into one field.

LINKED FIELDS FOR CONTEXT: where costed time should go against what taught the respondent's own moment. Id map: morning, advisor and observing map to watching; roleplay and classroom map to classroom; ops has no rank counterpart.

LINKED FIELDS FOR CONTEXT: what slowed Analysts on teams like yours against what a cohort peer who left before graduating lacked. Same option ids where the constructs match (clientbats, mix, and unclear/clarity); cohort_miss 'sponsor' has no h2_blocker counterpart. Both third person; reported as perceptions (Fisher 1993; Denrell 2003).

LINKED FIELDS FOR CONTEXT (Meade & Craig consistency pair, never quoted back): red_less 'format' or 'holdings' against where ai_swipe places 'Building the review pack'. Wanting Analysts freed from formatting packs while placing the pack on 'I do it' is coherent only if the respondent separates building the pack from formatting it. Report the rate; do not exclude.

weakestPoint:
1) Length is the formula's, not a stopwatch's. Every route is 36 cards and 414s (6.9 min): every branch sends each answer to a follow-up of the same seconds (three_year to took_ready, took_time or took_more; vote to one blue_*; red_how to class_mandatory or class_kept; cert to cert_how, cert_no or dep_cert; pace to one wrap_one_*), and simulate.test fails if any two routes differ by more than 10s or the longest exceeds mainPathSeconds. Text cards are timed as typed on a phone: moment 45s, wrap_more 30s. The rest uses the fatigue reviewer's formula: rank 4+2.5(n-1); swipe 4+2.5n; multi 6+1.2 per chip; tokens 4+5 per coloured token, or 2 per stacked block; pick 6 (four options or fewer) or 7; slider 7; ai_ladder 25. The title screen computes 'About 7 minutes'. Time five people on phones before sign-off.
2) Engine behaviour the content relies on (built and tested):
(a) Cards marked shuffle show their options in a per-respondent order drawn from a seed stored with the response and the card id, so every order can be rebuilt at analysis; catch-alls (other, none, nothing, never, notfreed) stay last (rule 14).
(b) vote has oneEach: the control refuses a second token of the same colour on one area, and isAnswered rejects it. faster and traits_rank still stack.
(c) h2_rank has max 3: the list shows a divider under the top three. The full order is still stored; read only the top three (Liang et al.).
(d) ai_ladder is drawn by LadderRungs (real text plus the LadderScene desk drawings), not an image slot, so it reads to a screen reader.
(e) Placed tokens show their label; a single-use token shows a tick once placed.
(f) The summit plays back the respondent's green areas, red_less, i2_central and wrap_one_* answers. No score, no badge.
(g) Still to build: title and cohort year from segmented invite links, cells under ten suppressed (rule 7), and a Details tap on the title screen: anonymous, graduates only, no group under ten, the survivorship note.
3) Deck and review items not carried, all for length:
- The vote is 2 green, 1 amber, 1 red, 1 blue, not the session's 3/2/2/1 (+15s). The readout must report each colour as shares of tokens, not raw counts, beside the session's tallies. The survey votes on six areas; the session votes on activities within them. Red is an area-level vote only; stem 2 ('spend less time on') is red_less, asked of everyone with six production tasks.
- 'Could the experience have happened earlier?' is not asked of the moment (+2.5s). The 'earlier' signals are three_year, h1_first and wrap_one 'Client exposure from week one'.
- h3_surprise stays a negative-only pick; 'where did you feel genuinely prepared' is carried only by p1_prep (a swipe over the six responsibilities would add 12s).
- Who gave the feedback (Advisor, manager, peer or recent grad, client) is not asked; i3_coach asks what it was about, and 'There wasn't any' shows where no one debriefed.
- then_now has no access partner card ('which first got you into a client conversation', +7s). Access is asked once, on the moment (h2_how 'It got me more client access').
- i2_ecm (what an Early Career Manager should track) is cut for length. D5's manager routines are covered by tagged ('Depends on their team and manager'), class_mandatory and i2_central.
- Adam's 'ready to do what?' is asked as took_ready of those ready at one or two; three_year's other stops get took_time (what a shorter A2A would have cost) or took_more (what was still missing), each 7s. Adam's 'more classroom, so mandatory?' is class_kept, worded from the respondent's own faster answer when they gave classroom a block; everyone else gets class_mandatory. Same option ids, one field.
4) Measurement limits that remain:
- p1_prep is the one global rating (peak-end; Sitzmann). Report it as 'graduates' overall mark', never as the headline, and nothing branches on it. Coded 1-5 so the stops are equally spaced.
- h2_rank is the one drag rank, kept because Adam asked for it by name; rule 8 prefers best-worst.
- Rule 6's 'a tool or example library could have taught me this faster' is not asked: it asks for an estimate of AI's effect on one's own development, which rule 7 bans. draft_next records behaviour on the last draft instead.
- Rule 10: there is no screener card. Instead no answer anywhere buys or saves a card.
- Survivorship: only graduates are asked. cohort_miss asks about a peer who left before graduating, in the third person; the readout must say findings describe what completers credit, not what works. Recommend a short parallel pulse with current Analysts and leavers.
5) Analysis: blue_* and wrap_one_* each merge into one field. The deck's four-level AI scale is read on ai_swipe: own = human-owned; assisted = human-led, AI-assisted; briefed and standing = AI-led with human review; service = reassign or self-serve. ai_swipe asks the highest rung a task could START at with the Analyst still learning to catch the planted error (evidence property 2), not who should do it. red_how adds reduce/automate/reassign/redesign for the red_less task. Final-call ownership is read from h2_how 'owncall' (the moment) and ai_swipe 'call' (the future).
6) Validation: checkGraph clean; graph.test word limits pass; simulate.test walks 1,000 respondents, none stranded, all 51 cards reached, every route 414s. e2e/flow.mjs walks seeded random routes in Chrome at 390px: all reach the summit, all 51 cards covered across ten routes, no overflow, no page errors. Not yet timed with people on phones.
